query: W melts near 3422 °C, whereas Cu boils near 2562 °C, so conventional induction or arc-plasma casting cannot readily yield a uniform W–Cu material. Phase separation and void formation can impair thermal transport. Filling a W skeleton with molten Cu or Cu powder can leave defects; spark-plasma sintering and mechanical alloying can produce finer, more uniform structures but can also leave voids; vapor-coated W powders have been sintered to achieve near-perfect contact between the constituents; and metal 3D printing has also been explored. Starting from W particles or connected W regions within a Cu matrix for heat transfer under irradiation in fusion-reactor joints, what single intervention could overcome these limitations while preserving mechanical durability? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts an outcome relative to a named existing fabrication baseline, defines the processing and service boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment and observations that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Liquid-metal dealloying of a Ti-containing precursor in molten Cu yields an aligned porous W scaffold that is uniformly infiltrated by Cu, thereby minimizing void formation and phase separation compared to conventional metal 3D printing.
generation.material_initial_state: A composite precursor consisting of W particles (or a connected W network) embedded in a Cu matrix with Ti-rich interdendritic regions that serve as a sacrificial phase.
generation.intervention: Immerse the Ti-containing W–Cu precursor in molten Cu at a temperature above the Cu melting point but well below any deleterious effects on W to enable selective dealloying of the Ti-rich channels.
generation.conditions: Processing in a molten Cu bath at controlled temperatures (above 1085 °C but below limits affecting W) and controlled time intervals to allow the liquid Cu to selectively remove Ti-rich regions without compromising the W scaffold.
generation.structural_mediator: An aligned, porous tungsten scaffold with nearly perfect interfacial contact with the Cu matrix and minimal void content.
generation.mechanism: The molten Cu preferentially dealloys Ti from the interdendritic regions, thereby both removing a potentially detrimental phase and permitting the Cu to fill the newly generated porous network. This enhanced wettability and continuity at the W-Cu interface reduces defects and improves thermal transport and mechanical durability.
generation.predicted_outcome: The liquid‐metal dealloyed W–Cu composite will exhibit reduced interfacial voids, improved thermal conductivity, and enhanced mechanical performance under irradiation relative to metal 3D printed W–Cu composites.
generation.baseline: Metal 3D printed W–Cu composites, which typically suffer from phase separation and void formation that impair thermal transport and mechanical durability.
generation.boundary: The intervention is applicable under processing temperatures where Cu remains molten but W integrity is maintained and for service conditions typical of fusion-reactor joints under irradiation and high thermal loads.
generation.uncertainty: The exact quantitative improvements in thermal transport and mechanical durability, as well as the complete elimination of voids, remain to be established through experimental testing.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one by applying liquid-metal dealloying on the Ti-containing W–Cu precursor and a control set via conventional metal 3D printing. Subject both sample sets to identical thermal treatment and simulated fusion-reactor irradiation conditions. Characterize the microstructure (e.g., via high-resolution electron microscopy) and measure thermal conductivity and mechanical (tensile) strength.
measurements: Interfacial void density and distribution via microscopy
Thermal conductivity tests under controlled heat flux
Mechanical strength tests such as tensile or flexural measurements
Irradiation performance metrics after simulated exposure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the liquid-metal dealloying samples do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in void content and corresponding improvements in thermal conductivity and mechanical durability compared to the 3D printed baseline, then the hypothesis is falsified.
